gaps.sentence: The tour included ___ visit to the British Museum.
gaps.explanation: 'A visit' (one of many possible) and 'the British Museum' (museums take 'the').

gaps.sentence: She works in ___ insurance, not banking.
gaps.explanation: Industry/sector names take no article: in insurance, in banking, in marketing.

gaps.sentence: The thief was sent to ___ prison for three years.
gaps.explanation: 'Sent to prison' — the institution, no article; 'the prison' would mean the building.

gaps.sentence: I downloaded ___ MP3 file from the band's website.
gaps.explanation: 'MP3' is pronounced /em/, a vowel sound, so 'an'.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ best film of the decade by common consent.
___ Smith family have lived in this street since 1990.
gaps.explanation: 'The Smith family' — the whole family takes 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: She works as ___ editor for a travel magazine.
